title: Which decimal is closest to one, and which to one point zero nine?
description: From 0.9, 1.1, 1.01 and 1.11 we find the decimal closest to 1 and then the one closest to 1.09, by finding every gap. Keeko doubts the first answer and thinks 0.9 is closest to 1.
teaching_notes: One idea: the closest number has the smallest gap, so find every gap and compare. Watch for students who pick a number by how it looks.

source: Which of 0.9, 1.1, 1.01 and 1.11 is closest to 1? Then which
video_script.why: The child can compare decimals and now measures how far each one lies from a target.
video_script.substitution: Find the gap between each decimal and the target, larger minus smaller, and pick the smallest gap.
video_script.anchor: the decimals 0.9, 1.1, 1.01 and 1.11 on a number line around 1 and 1.09
video_script.wrong_move: Picks 0.9 as closest to 1 without finding every gap.
video_script.payoff_line: Find every gap and pick the smallest

final_answer.value: 1.01 is closest to 1; 1.1 is closest to 1.09
final_answer.spoken: one point zero one is closest to one; one point one is closest to one point zero nine

hold_back: 1.01 is closest to 1; 1.1 is closest to 1.09
video_script.design: The four decimals sit on a number line. For each target, a bracket shows the gap to each decimal, and the shortest bracket is highlighted.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a number line with 0.9, 1, 1.01, 1.09, 1.1 and 1.11 marked

marks.four: the four decimals appear on the line
marks.ask: the targets one and one point zero nine are marked

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about closest decimals.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Four decimals are given. They are zero point nine, one point one, one point zero one, and one point one one.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which is closest to one? Which is closest to one point zero nine?

beats.on_screen: the number line with the four decimals stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the end of the number line

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: gap = larger number - smaller number; closest = smallest gap

marks.gap: a bracket joins two numbers on the line

narration: <bookmark mark='gap'/>A gap is how far apart two numbers are, found as the larger minus the smaller.
<bookmark mark='small'/>The closest number has the smallest gap.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the four decimals from the line.
<bookmark mark='targets'/>The targets are one, and one point zero nine.

beats.on_screen: To find: the decimal closest to each target
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the closest decimal for each target.

marks.a: the gap to zero point nine is written
marks.b: the gap to one point one is written
marks.c: the gaps to the last two are written

narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step one, find each gap from one, starting with zero point nine, which is zero point one away.
<bookmark mark='b'/>One point one is zero point one away.
<bookmark mark='c'/>One point zero one is zero point zero one away. One point one one is zero point one one away.

beats.on_screen: smallest gap 0.01, so 1.01 is closest to 1

marks.small: the gap zero point zero one is circled
marks.pick: one point zero one is ticked

narration: <bookmark mark='small'/>Step two, pick the smallest gap, which is zero point zero one.
<bookmark mark='pick'/>That belongs to one point zero one.

marks.a: the gap to zero point nine is written
marks.b: the gap to one point one is written
marks.c: the gaps to the last two are written

narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Step three, find each gap from one point zero nine. Zero point nine is zero point one nine away.
<bookmark mark='b'/>One point one is zero point zero one away.
<bookmark mark='c'/>One point zero one is zero point zero eight away. One point one one is zero point zero two away.

beats.on_screen: smallest gap 0.01, so 1.1 is closest to 1.09

marks.small: the gap zero point zero one is circled

narration: <bookmark mark='small'/>Step four, pick the smallest gap, which is zero point zero one.
<bookmark mark='pick'/>That belongs to one point one.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 1.01 is closest to 1; 1.1 is closest to 1.09

marks.vals: the two closest decimals are ticked on the line

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Find every gap and pick the smallest.
<bookmark mark='vals'/>One point zero one is closest to one. One point one is closest to one point zero nine.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the number line
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a speech bubble: 0.9 is closest to 1; 0.9 is 0.1 below 1 but 1.01 is only 0.01 above; the bubble is crossed out

marks.fix: the two gaps are shown side by side

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks zero point nine is closest, since it looks so near.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But it is zero point one below one. And one point zero one is only zero point zero one above.
<bookmark mark='all'/>We must find every gap before we decide.
